frequency_question: How often do threatened major bilateral tariffs proceed to implementation within the stated window rather than being rescinded or replaced by a deal?
membership_rule: Includes explicitly threatened, high-magnitude tariffs between developed trading partners with integrated supply chains where a specific future implementation deadline was established. Excludes broad multi-lateral WTO dispute tariffs or minor antidumping duties.

cases.name: US Threat of Tariffs on Mexico over Border Security
US Threat of Tariffs on European Steel and Aluminum

coverage_note: 3 named key precedent episodes involving executive-level tariff threats for leverage.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller-scale administrative trade cases handled purely through bureaucratic channels.
skeleton: Threatened trade friction episodes with specific executive deadlines since 1980, categorized by whether leverage was used to extract concessions (miss) or executed as policy (hit).
multiplier: 2 hits out of 3 major distinct high-level North American/Western bilateral escalation episodes.
validity_reason: Executive trade policy posture and negotiation tactics remain consistent across this political cycle.
